log.text: Liftoff. The Moon in the window: 30° right. Fuel for 48 s of burn.
Target centred in the window (+2°). DNp20: right 0 Hz, left 0 Hz.
Out of the dense air: altitude 36, speed 16 u/s.
Meteor M-1 in the window (41° right, 30% of the Moon's light). The pilot held its course.
The Moon is blinding. The retina turns its sensitivity down to 48%.
Target held centred for 11.2 s without a break.
Flight computer: flip, engines first. Altitude 164, closing 40 u/s. The pilot's lever is off for the manoeuvre.
Meteor M-6 in the window (3° left, 21% of the Moon's light). The pilot turned toward its light: the target slid to 176° left.
Flip complete, landing burn. The pilot now looks through the landing camera; its lever moves the rocket sideways.
Pad centred in the landing camera (+3°), altitude 84.
Flight computer: altitude 20. Below this the sideways speed is limited in proportion to height; the direction stays the pilot's.
Touchdown: 1.5 u/s down, 0.3 u/s sideways, ground slope 16°, 3.7 u from the centre of the pad.

The legs' signal reached 2,522 leg mechanosensory neurons. In 0.5 s the ascending neurons (legs → brain) fired 16,224 spikes, against 0 before contact. Strongest in the brain: PEN_a(PEN1) (+1,829), PEN_b(PEN2) (+1,740), cells with no named type (+1,391).

cause: CAUSE: the rocket tipped over after touchdown — ground slope 16°, above the 12° the legs can stand on. The pad was 4 u away.
